author: TEDx Talks
description:
Why belonging feels risky, and five brave choices that shift it from something you hope others grant into a practice you cultivate. Reut Schwartz-Hebron is the founder of KCI (Key Change Institute) and a neuroscience-obsessed expert in human change, focused on transformation where it actually happens: inside the brain. For more than two decades, she has trained and certified hundreds of executive and life coaches in Advanced Applied Neuroscience, so they can support their coaching clients tackle one enduring human puzzle: why we struggle to adopt the changes we genuinely want. 

Beyond working with experienced coaches, Reut has coached brains and the people who belong to them across a wide range of settings, from elite military teams to Fortune 500 companies including Comcast, Phillips, and GSK. She is known for translating complex neuroscience into practical tools, and has written books and numerous articles on unlearning and difficult change, illuminating what’s really going on in t
title: How to belong without losing yourself | Reut Schwartz-Hebron | TEDxManitou Springs Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
You worked hard. Followed the advice. Then your career took a turn you never planned. Margaret Weniger went looking for what she’d done wrong. Hundreds of interviews later, she began to question the question itself. Margaret Weniger is challenging one of our most persistent ideas about work: that a successful career follows a predictable path.

After 12 years climbing the technology sales ladder, Margaret began studying what happens when carefully made career plans collide with layoffs, changing priorities and unexpected turns. Her research with professionals revealed that career disruption was far less unusual than we’ve been taught to believe. Her own experience gave the question particular urgency: Behind a résumé that looked successful, Margaret had been fired and laid off multiple times. 

Today, Margaret is director of Startup Launch at Georgia Tech’s CREATE-X, where she helps founders navigate uncertainty and build companies. She is also the author of “Broken: Designing Careers
title: Are we asking the wrong questions after a career setback? | Margaret Weniger | TEDxAtlanta

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if some of the world's most powerful solutions are already here, held in the wisdom of women whose voices too often go unheard?

When Ronda Carnegie gathered a circle of women to share what they wished they'd known at 16 with her young daughter, she discovered something that would take her across continents: knowledge can change lives, but trust and connection are what allow it to change the world.

From India and Ethiopia to Uganda and Colombia, Ronda reveals what becomes possible when women share what they know — and why the future may depend less on finding new answers than on recognizing the wisdom already among us. Ronda Carnegie is the Co-Founder and Executive Director of Project Dandelion, a global, women-led initiative that mobilizes collective leadership for a climate-safe, livable world. As a member of TED's leadership team, she helped transform TED from a conference into a global platform for ideas by building global partnerships, co-founding TEDWomen, and creating the
title: The Hidden Power of Women Sharing What They Know | Ronda Carnegie | TEDxAmazônia

author: TEDx Talks
description: Christina Joymon reframes gender equality in the workplace, asking if the real answer starts closer to home than we think. Christina Elizabeth Joymon is an engineer, investor, award-winning author, and global speaker bridging technology, entrepreneurship, leadership, and the arts. As Founder and General Partner of XIA Capital, she has spent over a decade investing in AI, sustainability, and women-led ventures, while advocating for women in STEM through ASME's Women's Leadership Collective and Project Aspire. She's also the award-winning novelist behind Royal Planet. Sparked by a defining classroom moment as a female engineering student, Christina's talk asks what it will really take to move the needle on gender equality — and why the answer may start closer to home than we think. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Equality Isn't a Policy. It's a Practice We Teach at Home. | Christina Joymon | TEDxABQ

author: TEDx Talks
description: Dr. Sahgee reframes the future of medicine, asking what happens when AI catches illness months before diagnosis. Dr. Sageline LaBaze, known as Dr. Sahgee, is a first-generation Haitian American physician, a Preventive Medicine and Public Health resident at the University of New Mexico, and an MPH candidate at Johns Hopkins. Founder of Solterix Inc. and Solterica AI, she merges artificial intelligence with preventive health to dismantle systemic barriers before they become diagnoses. Her talk poses a striking question: what if your doctor knew you were getting sick months before you did? Drawing on her clinical experience and New Mexico's unique healthcare challenges, Dr. Sahgee explores where AI in medicine is headed next — and why it matters for all of us. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Quantum Wellness: The Better Use for AI in Healthcare | Dr. Sageline LaBaze | TEDxABQ

author: TEDx Talks
description: Anastasia Zagrai reframes who's equipped to inspire future scientists, asking if it's not the experts we'd expect at all. Anastasia Zagrai is a recent graduate of Socorro High School in rural New Mexico and an incoming civil engineering student at MIT. As an engineering researcher, Science Olympiad competitor, and founder of Socorro Sparks, she creates hands-on STEM experiences for local students. Anastasia believes students are often held back not by lack of interest, but by fear of being wrong. Drawing on her experience teaching rural youth through Socorro Sparks, her talk asks a provocative question: what if the people best equipped to inspire the next generation of scientists and engineers aren't who we expect at all? This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The Overlooked Kid Who Became the Role Model She Needed | Anastasia Zagrai | TEDxABQ

author: TEDx Talks
description: Miranda Garcia reframes teen stress, drawing on her own research to ask what we're getting wrong about supporting teenagers. Miranda Garcia is a senior at V. Sue Cleveland High School in Rio Rancho, New Mexico, whose STEM journey has taken her through Girls Who Code, Young Women in Computing, STEM Mavericks, and Higher Orbits' Go For Launch. She has engineered a seizure detection and alert system using a Raspberry Pi and conducted award-winning research on how breathing techniques affect stressed teenagers, alongside teaching STEM as an Education and Outreach Intern at R4 Creating. This fall she heads to New Mexico State University to study Chemical and Materials Engineering. In her talk, Miranda draws on her own research to ask what we might be getting wrong about how we support teenagers today. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Rethinking teenage stress | Miranda Garcia | TEDxABQ

author: TEDx Talks
description: Mary Beth Lindsey reframes sexual assault as everyone's public health crisis, not just the demographic left to fix it. Mary Beth Lindsey is an actor, singer, performer, and community advocate serving as Education & Prevention Manager for Solace Sexual Assault Services in Santa Fe, where she's also a well-known local emcee performing as Miss Anita Whiskey. In her talk, Mary Beth points to a striking disconnect: the professionals leading sexual assault recovery work are rarely the demographic most often responsible for perpetrating it. Drawing on CDC research, she makes the case for a different, more coordinated response to what she argues is a public health crisis touching all of us. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: We Have to Work Together to Prevent Sexual Violence  | Mary Beth Lindsey | TEDxABQ

author: TEDx Talks
description: Samantha Schwann reframes exploration itself, showing how advancing ROV tech is expanding what the ocean can teach us. Samantha Schwann is an underwater visual artist and explorer working at the intersection of exploration, technology, and conservation. A member of The Explorer's Club, she pilots a remotely operated vehicle (ROV) to document biodiversity in the ocean's low-light “twilight zone,” where only a fraction of sunlight reaches. In her talk, Samantha shares findings from seven progressively challenging ROV expeditions into a submarine canyon, revealing hidden biodiversity and surprising marine events in an otherwise well-documented protected environment. As ROV technology advances, she shows how our understanding of the ocean's least-observed places is only beginning to unfold. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: You Don't Need to Dive to Discover | Samantha Schwann | TEDxABQ

author: TEDx Talks
description: From stage fright to Vienna's stages, Elizabeth Garland reframes confidence for introverts with what she calls Superpresence. Elizabeth Garland is an international composer, performer, educator, and performance coach who has performed at the World Composers Concert in Vienna, served as artist-in-residence at the Santa Fe Art Institute, and won honors including First Prize in the Unsigned Only Instrumental Competition. Her writing appears in the bestselling Power of Why series. Drawing on her own journey from stage fright to Vienna's concert halls, Elizabeth's talk challenges what sensitive, introverted performers are typically told about confidence — and introduces a different way forward she calls Superpresence. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Performance isn't Projection. It's Connection. | Elizabeth Garland | TEDxABQ

author: TEDx Talks
description: Eddie Tafoya reframes a lifetime of falling short of perfection, making the case that our flaws are exactly what the world needs. Eddie Tafoya is an Albuquerque native, English professor, author, and comedian featured in A&E's docuseries The Right to Offend: A Look at African American Comedy. His books include The Legacy of the Wisecrack, Icons of African American Comedy, and the novel Finding the Buddha, with The Marxist Revolution: How Chico, Harpo, Groucho, and Zeppo Changed the Way We Laugh releasing in 2027. In his talk, Eddie takes on a lifetime of messages about falling short of perfection — and makes an unexpected case for why our flaws might be exactly what the world needs from us. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Confessions of a Serial Failure | Eddie Tafoya | TEDxABQ

author: TEDx Talks
description: Jaime Campbell reframes what it takes to see someone as a whole person, drawn from her own story of diagnosis and love. Jaime Campbell is a Certified Peer Support Worker and disability advocate who began volunteering with children with disabilities at age 12, learning ASL along the way. At 19, she began her own journey with schizophrenia. After marrying her husband Jon, who lived with autism and psychosis and passed away due to gaps in specialized care, Jaime committed herself to bridging the mental illness and developmental disability communities. She's now completing her MSW. Her talk walks through her own story of diagnosis and love, and asks what it really takes to see someone as a whole person. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Crazy in Love | Jaime Campbell | TEDxABQ

author: TEDx Talks
description: Our relationships and surroundings shape our motivation and sense of possibility. Contrary to many people's belief, low motivation isn't a fixed personality trait. Instead, we can design our own outcomes by intentionally seeking out people and environments that help us realize our potential. Junior at Design Tech High School This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Beyond the Bare Minimum | Freya Schecter | TEDxDesign Tech HS

author: TEDx Talks
description: Jon Sakura reframes gaming from a solitary screen-lit activity into something built around people, not just play. Jon Sakura is a small business owner born and raised in Albuquerque, where he runs a local gaming cafe built around community, alongside passions for music, drawing, and cats. His talk takes a second look at what we assume video gaming has to be — a solitary, screen-lit activity — and makes the case for something different. Jon shares his vision for what gaming spaces could look like when they're built around people instead of just play. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Nostalgic for a connection WIFI can't give | Jon Sakura | TEDxABQ

author: TEDx Talks
description:
A small act of encouragement can change what a person believes is possible. Drawing on a teacher’s recognition of her potential during a period of self-doubt, this talk argues that belief and support help people act on abilities they already possess.  I’m a high school student passionate about creativity, community impact, and designing meaningful experiences. Whether I’m leading a project, building a game concept, developing an app, or running a kindness-centered club, I care about solving real problems in innovative, human-centered ways.

I’m the founder of Bracelet Making Connection: Givers Get Club, an initiative focused on combating loneliness and exclusion at my school by anonymously creating bracelets for every student. Through this project, I’ve built skills in project management, organization, team leadership, and community engagement.

I've collaborated with National Geographic on a youth innovation challenge, designing a narrative survival game that teaches an explorer mind
title: Small Words, Big Possibilities | Luciana OrRico Gomes | TEDxDesign Tech HS

author: TEDx Talks
description: Author Saleema Ishq reframes her strangest, most hidden fears as the surprising secret behind her thriller-writing career. Saleema Ishq is a psychological thriller author whose debut novel, Sisters Arcana, was a finalist for the New Mexico Book Awards and nominated for Best Thriller in the Indieverse Awards. A two-time Top 5 nominee for Top Author in the New Mexico Entertainment Awards, her forthcoming thriller Dig Deeper releases Fall 2026. In her talk, Saleema opens up about a lifelong struggle with existential fears too strange and uncomfortable to share — and reveals the surprising role those very fears have played in shaping her career. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Stop Killing Your Darlings | Saleema Ishq | TEDxABQ

author: TEDx Talks
description: A TEDx talk titled "Journey from Confusion to Self-Discovery" explores how moments of uncertainty, self-doubt, and life detours are not obstacles, but essential catalysts for growth. Rather than viewing confusion as a sign of being lost, the talk frames it as an invitation to question inherited beliefs, re-examine identity, and peel back external expectations.  Gaurav Mathur is a professional wedding anchor and emcee with a diverse background in music, sports, and corporate leadership. A former HR professional with experience at startups like Josh Talks and Thrillophilia, he began his anchoring career in 2015 and has hosted 2,000+ luxury weddings, destination events, and corporate shows across India and internationally. He was honoured with the “Most Versatile Wedding Anchor of the Year” award by WIVA Awards. His journey inspires young people to explore their passions and turn them into meaningful careers. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but indepen
title: Journey from Confusion to Self Discovery | Gaurav Mathur | TEDxMaheswari Public School Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: The Next Chapter aims to inspire high schoolers, who are often stressed about their next steps, whether working on their college applications or beginning to think about their future pathways. Camila describes how she accepted different versions of herself, explored her various passions, and never backed down from setbacks. Guiding students through her journey that ultimately led her to found her company, she encourages students to explore different pathways in high school and believe in themselves, even when things are hard.  Camila Sáenz is the Founder of TUTEEMI, an EdTech platform connecting +150 foreign language tutors with Taiwanese students in person, and the Founder of OutliersGT, a community of globally minded leaders driving change in Guatemala. She is also a Ph.D. candidate in Business Management at National Taipei University of Technology, where her research focuses on gender equality in executive leadership, exploring how cultural norms and organizational practices shape
title: The Next Chapter - Camila Sáenz | Camilia Sáenz | TEDxAS Taichung Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
La vita d’artista e da musicista non è sempre champagne e supernove: a volte deviamo la direzione, cambiamo nome, progetto, ci innamoriamo o ci perdiamo. Tra canzoni dal vivo, installazioni artistiche e stelle che collassano, Zara Colombo — il duo formato da Zara C. Massaro e Luca Massaro — ci raccontano del loro primo album pubblicato da Sugar, il loro tour e il dialogo costante tra immagine e musica. A volte bisogna sbandare per cambiare direzione, sparire per trovarsi, degenerare per generare: cercare una fotografia tra i tasti bianchi e neri di un piano, una luce nel buco nero di una chitarra. Cosa succede quando l’arte visiva incontra la musica? Nasce Zara Colombo , il duo formato dalla cantante italo-argentina Zara C. Massaro e dal compositore e artista visuale Luca Massaro.
Dall’unione tra parola, immagine e suono prende vita un progetto poliedrico che intreccia radici patagoniche, moda e arte contemporanea. Sul palco di TEDx Barletta ci guidano in un viaggio unico tra linguagg
title: Stelle Degeneri - Sparire dentro a una canzone | Zara Colombo | TEDxBarletta

author: TEDx Talks
description:
È davvero possibile trovare la forza di rinascere nei momenti di massima oscurità?
In questa performance, scritta in collaborazione con Andrea Cincotti, Vanillivia ci racconta come la fine di un ciclo possa trasformarsi nell'inizio di qualcosa di straordinario. Attraverso la metafora cosmica della Supernova, ci accompagna in un viaggio intimo tra vulnerabilità, coraggio e rinascita, perché a volte, per poter splendere, bisogna prima avere il coraggio di lasciarsi andare. Matteo Candido, studente di scenografia all’Accademia di Belle Arti di Bari, trova la sua massima espressione in Vanillivia, l'alter ego scenico creato 5 anni fa.
L'intero percorso di Matteo è stato una preparazione alla nascita di questo personaggio. Cresciuto respirando la magia del "dietro le quinte", è rimasto stregato dal mondo teatrale, tra costumi, scene e parrucche. Questo universo visivo si è intrecciato profondamente alla sua formazione musicale e alla passione per il canto ereditata dalla famiglia, che tutt
title: Non tutte le morti sono una fine | Vanillivia  | TEDxBarletta

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Dalla potenza di una stella che collassa nasce la vita; dalla ricerca interiore e dal desiderio di comprendere il caos nasce la musica. Voce tra le più raffinate della nuova scena R&B e Soul italiana, Lauryyn (Aurora De Gregorio) trasforma l’introspezione personale nel racconto di un’intera generazione.
Dalla colonna sonora di Skam Italia fino alla finale delle Targhe Tenco con il suo album Aritmia, la cantautrice pugliese unisce sonorità internazionali e testi intensi. Al TEDxBarletta ci farà scoprire la forza di dare voce alle proprie fragilità. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Esplodere per creare | Lauryyn  | TEDxBarletta

author: TEDx Talks
description: Perché proviamo così tanto timore nell'ammettere di non sapere qualcosa? E soprattutto, perché è importante spiegare qualcosa a chi è ignorante? Partendo da un ricordo d'infanzia, Enrico Gamba ci guida in una riflessione profonda sulla scuola e l'inaccessibilità della cultura. Un racconto intimo e illuminante che mette in discussione il nozionismo e ci ricorda che la conoscenza ha davvero senso solo quando riesce a essere alla portata di tutti. Enrico Gamba, noto come 151eg, è uno dei creator più seguiti in Italia nel settore del cinema e dell’animazione. Dal 2011, attraverso il suo canale YouTube, condivide analisi approfondite, curiosità e retroscena di film, serie animate e opere cinematografiche, coinvolgendo una community appassionata e in costante crescita. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Perché mio padre non sapeva cosa fosse una Supernova | Enrico Gamba | TEDxBarletta

author: TEDx Talks
description: Non possiamo scegliere la tempesta. Ma possiamo imparare a nuotare. Cosa succede quando la vita cambia improvvisamente e tutto ciò che pensavamo di essere viene messo in discussione? Carlo Calcagni, Colonnello, ex pilota militare e atleta paralimpico, porta sul palco di TEDxBarletta una riflessione sul significato più profondo della parola "scegliere". Dopo aver affrontato gravi problemi di salute, dolore e limitazioni fisiche, Carlo ha imparato a guardare la propria esistenza attraverso una domanda diversa: non più «Perché proprio a me?», ma «Adesso che è successo, cosa scelgo di farne?». Dal ritorno allo sport attraverso il frame running alla scoperta della forza delle relazioni, il suo racconto ci invita a ripensare il rapporto con i nostri limiti, con la fragilità e con il tempo che abbiamo a disposizione. Perché accettare non significa arrendersi. E la vera forza non consiste necessariamente nell'affrontare tutto da soli, ma anche nel saper chiedere aiuto, amare e trasformare la
title: Imparare a nuotare nella tempesta | Carlo Calcagni | TEDxBarletta

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Some of humanity's greatest breakthroughs have come with costs no one anticipated.
History offers a striking example: a century ago, an inventor inhaled chemical fumes in front of reporters to demonstrate their safety. His breakthroughs solved major problems of their time, yet their unintended consequences would harm millions across generations, often in ways that were difficult to see, feel, or trace.
As artificial intelligence reshapes our lives and our planet, are we repeating the same mistakes?
AI and energy entrepreneur Hadi Ganjineh explores the hidden costs of technological progress, from AI's impact on human identity and purpose to the growing energy demands of hyperscale data centers.
At the heart of his talk is the concept of "slow violence," developed by Rob Nixon: harm that unfolds gradually, across time and distance, often beyond our immediate awareness.
But what if the very technology creating these challenges could also help solve them? Drawing on AI's potential to anal
title: Can AI Outsmart Itself? The Harm We Can't See | Hadi Ganjineh | TEDxSaigon

author: TEDx Talks
description: "Komm zurück zu deinen Wurzeln.“ Diesen Satz hört Nicole Marquardt seit Jahren, und er lässt sie mit einer Frage zurück. Ein persönlicher Talk über Heimat, Zuhause, Zugehörigkeit und das, was wir unter Wurzeln verstehen. Nicole Marquardt spent thirty years in large international organizations, leading complex projects for global clients, usually under high pressure. Today she lives between two continents and writes books. What drives her is the connection to people, to stories, to cultures. When she is not writing, you will find her playing tennis, out in nature or cooking with friends. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Wo Wurzeln wirklich wachsen | Nicole Marquardt | TEDxBruneck

author: TEDx Talks
description: In Südtirol ist niemand selbstverständlich die Norm: Wer deutschsprachig ist, gehört im Land zur Mehrheit und im Staat zur Minderheit, und umgekehrt. Joachim Goller ist in Bruneck aufgewachsen und lebt heute in New York. Er erzählt, was eine Kindheit ohne Standardeinstellung mit einem Menschen macht, und nimmt das Publikum mit nach Kanada, nach Mexiko und zu den Südtirolerinnen und Südtirolern, die ins Ausland gegangen sind. Was passiert, wenn niemand mehr die Norm ist? Ein Talk über Identität, Mehrsprachigkeit, Minderheiten, Auswanderung und die Fähigkeit, sich anzupassen, in einer Welt, die ihr Zentrum verliert. Joachim Goller grew up in Bruneck and lives in New York, where he works as a manager at the logistics group Kuehne+Nagel and is a member of the Südstern network. What drives him is curiosity about the unfamiliar: new contexts, new connections, new ways of looking at a problem. When he is not traveling, his day almost always starts the same way, in the gym or on a run along t
title: Nie die Norm, immer im Vorteil | Joachim Goller | TEDxBruneck

author: TEDx Talks
description: Descrição: E se a metodologia que usamos para inovar produtos e serviços pudesse transformar a nossa própria vida? Isabel Novais Machado, diretora de design, aplica o design thinking àquilo que mais importa: nós próprios. Pergunta se caminhamos na direção do que nos faz felizes, ou apenas ao ritmo que o mundo escolheu por nós. E chega ao passo mais simples e mais difícil de todos: parar. Isabel Novais Machado é líder de design com mais de 15 anos de experiência em estratégia, design thinking e inovação tecnológica, em startups, multinacionais e scale-ups. Apaixonada por neurociências e desenvolvimento humano, é também podcaster, professora e mentora. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Design thinking para a vida | Isabel Novais Machado | TEDxAveiro

author: TEDx Talks
description: Quando é que uma parede pintada deixa de ser vandalismo e passa a ser arte? EDIS ONE, artista urbano, parte do seu percurso do graffiti aos murais de grande escala para refletir sobre a fronteira entre o que a sociedade condena e o que acaba por celebrar. E sobre o papel da arte na relação entre a humanidade e a natureza. EDIS ONE é um artista urbano português que usa a arte para refletir sobre sustentabilidade, extinção de espécies e a relação entre a humanidade e a natureza. Em 2016 criou o maior mural do mundo que brilha no escuro, nos Emirados Árabes Unidos, um recorde do Guinness. É fundador do Original Extinction Art Project e embaixador da ANP | WWF desde 2019. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Ilegal até ser arte | Edis One | TEDxAveiro

author: TEDx Talks
description: A solidão nas pessoas mais velhas é uma realidade muitas vezes invisível, mas com consequências profundas para a saúde, a dignidade e a coesão social. Ângelo Valente e Nídia Matos, da Associação Extragenária, partilham experiências concretas no terreno que mostram como é possível reconstruir ligações e devolver o sentido de pertença a quem se sente esquecido. Um testemunho real mostra como pequenas mudanças podem transformar uma vida. Ângelo Valente e Nídia Matos trazem duas perspetivas complementares: a de quem cria e a de quem vive a transformação. Através da Associação Extragenária, desenvolvem uma intervenção que cruza cultura, participação e comunidade, reforçando o sentido de pertença e a ligação entre pessoas mais velhas. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: O barulho do silêncio | Ângelo Valente | TEDxAveiro

author: TEDx Talks
description: Warum treffen manche Menschen Entscheidungen in Sekunden und andere scheitern an einer Kugel Eis? Valeria Told zeigt, was in uns entscheidet: nicht Logik und keine Pro-und-Contra-Listen, sondern innere Bilder und das Gefühl, das sie im Körper auslösen. An Entscheidungen, die ihr Leben verändert haben, erklärt sie, wie diese Bilder entstehen, warum sie dich unterstützen oder auch nicht und wie du ein Bild verändern kannst, das dich blockiert. Valeria Told comes from Meran, her father from Antholz, where she spent her childhood summers. In her late twenties she took over as director of the Haydn Orchestra of Bozen and Trient in 2010 and led it for eleven years. She then ran the theater festival at the Teatro Greco in Syracuse and founded a European education company for classical music. She followed love to Germany and her inner calling to Portugal, where she lives today, writes and tends a meditation garden claimed by two cats. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conferen
title: Vanille oder Schokolade? Was in dir entscheidet | Valeria Told | TEDxBruneck

author: TEDx Talks
description: Die Intelligenz wird austauschbar, der Kontext bleibt. Warum der nächste große Schritt nicht der bessere Chatbot ist, sondern ein Computer, den wir nicht mehr bedienen müssen. Heutige KI-Systeme fragen, antworten und warten wieder. Markus Ertel zeigt, was einem Computer fehlt, damit er über längere Zeit sinnvoll handeln kann: ein Gedächtnis, das nicht mit jeder Unterhaltung neu beginnt, Ziele, die er behält, und die Fähigkeit, Wissen von Vermutungen zu unterscheiden. Ein Talk über künstliche Intelligenz, Cognitive Computing und die Zukunft unserer Arbeit mit Technik. Markus Ertel lives in Magdalensberg in Carinthia and has family in Bruneck. He develops generative artificial intelligence that runs locally and complies with data protection law, as a counter-model to the large systems from the USA and China. He is interested in how biological systems can be translated into technical ones, for example the human memory into the architecture of a piece of software. This talk was given at a
title: Wir müssen Computer nicht mehr bedienen: Cognitive Computing | Markus Ertel | TEDxBruneck
